mock_answer_response.answer_text: [SYNTHETIC MOCK ANSWER] In India, a classical Ayurvedic formulation manufactured strictly according to an authoritative text listed in the First Schedule of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 is categorized as a Classical ASU Drug under Section 3(a). Furthermore, under Section 3(p) of the Patents Act, 1970, an invention which in effect is traditional knowledge or an aggregation of known properties of traditionally known components is not patentable.
assumptions: Assumed all ingredients are known classical herbs listed in official pharmacopoeia.
Assumed no synthetic chemical additives or modified solvent fractions are introduced.
